quests.hint: It follows 'I'd' to show which of two options you prefer.
quests.explanation: 'I'd rather + base verb + than + base verb' expresses preference: 'I'd rather stay than go'. There is no 'to' after rather.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd ___ stay in tonight than go to the party; I'm exhausted.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd rather stay in tonight than go to the party; I'm exhausted.
quests.contextClue: 'Than go' contrasts the two options, and exhaustion explains the choice.

quests.hint: Someone who likes something a lot.
quests.explanation: 'A big fan of' + noun shows strong liking. 'Not really a big fan' is a polite way to say you dislike something.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not really a big ___ of horror films; they give me nightmares.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm not really a big fan of horror films; they give me nightmares.
quests.contextClue: Nightmares explain why the speaker avoids the genre.

quests.hint: Tolerate or put up with.
quests.explanation: 'Can't stand' + noun or -ing means dislike very strongly: 'can't stand waiting'. It is stronger than 'don't like'.
quests.textToSpeak: My brother can't ___ the smell of fish, so we never cook it at home.
quests.correctAnswer: My brother can't stand the smell of fish, so we never cook it at home.
quests.contextClue: Never cooking fish shows a strong dislike.

quests.hint: What you personally think about something.
quests.explanation: 'In my opinion' introduces your own view. Similar openers: 'In my view', 'As far as I'm concerned'.
quests.textToSpeak: In my ___, the first version of the logo looks much better.
quests.correctAnswer: In my opinion, the first version of the logo looks much better.
quests.contextClue: The speaker gives a personal judgment about two logos.

quests.hint: The verb for having a view in your mind.
quests.explanation: English usually puts the negative on 'think': 'I don't think it's a good idea', not 'I think it isn't a good idea'. It sounds softer.
quests.textToSpeak: I don't ___ it's a good idea to drive in this snow.
quests.correctAnswer: I don't think it's a good idea to drive in this snow.
quests.contextClue: A softened disagreement about driving in snow.

quests.hint: Truthful and open.
quests.explanation: 'To be honest' introduces a frank opinion, often a slightly negative one. It prepares the listener for what follows.
quests.textToSpeak: To be ___, I didn't enjoy the film very much.
quests.correctAnswer: To be honest, I didn't enjoy the film very much.
quests.contextClue: A negative opinion is being introduced frankly.

quests.hint: Correct.
quests.explanation: 'You're right' agrees that someone is correct. 'Absolutely' strengthens it. The opposite is 'You're wrong'.
quests.textToSpeak: You're absolutely ___. I should have listened to you earlier.
quests.correctAnswer: You're absolutely right. I should have listened to you earlier.
quests.contextClue: The speaker admits they should have listened.

quests.hint: Share the same opinion.
quests.explanation: 'I couldn't agree more' is a fixed phrase meaning you agree completely. The negative form gives a strong positive meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: That's exactly what I was thinking! I couldn't ___ more.
quests.correctAnswer: That's exactly what I was thinking! I couldn't agree more.
quests.contextClue: 'Exactly what I was thinking' shows total shared opinion.

quests.hint: Sufficient.
quests.explanation: 'Fair enough' is a casual reply meaning 'that seems reasonable'. It accepts a point without strong enthusiasm.
quests.textToSpeak: You want to leave early because of the traffic? Fair ___.
quests.correctAnswer: You want to leave early because of the traffic? Fair enough.
quests.contextClue: The speaker accepts the reason that was just given.

quests.hint: Have a different opinion from someone.
quests.explanation: 'Disagree with someone' takes 'with'. The noun is 'disagreement'. 'I'm sorry, but' softens the opposing view.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm sorry, but I have to ___ with you; the plan will cost too much.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm sorry, but I have to disagree with you; the plan will cost too much.
quests.contextClue: An apology followed by a cost objection signals a polite opposing view.

quests.hint: A reasonable argument that someone has made.
quests.explanation: 'That's a fair point' or 'good point' acknowledges an argument before you add your own view. 'But' often follows.
quests.textToSpeak: That's a fair ___, but I still think we should ask them first.
quests.correctAnswer: That's a fair point, but I still think we should ask them first.
quests.contextClue: 'But I still think' shows the speaker accepts something and keeps their view.

quests.hint: Certain.
quests.explanation: 'I'm not sure' is a mild, polite way to show doubt or disagree. It sounds softer than 'you're wrong'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm not so ___ about that. Maybe we should check the map first.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm not so sure about that. Maybe we should check the map first.
quests.contextClue: 'Maybe we should check' shows doubt.

quests.hint: Accept something as true.
quests.explanation: 'I can't believe it!' expresses surprise. It can be followed by a noun or a clause: 'I can't believe you won.'
quests.textToSpeak: You won a holiday? I can't ___ it!
quests.correctAnswer: You won a holiday? I can't believe it!
quests.contextClue: Surprising news prompts disbelief.

quests.hint: The word you use to show sympathy for bad news.
quests.explanation: 'Sorry to hear' + news is a response to bad news: 'I'm sorry to hear that.' It does not mean you did anything wrong.
quests.textToSpeak: Oh no, that's terrible. I'm so ___ to hear about your grandmother.
quests.correctAnswer: Oh no, that's terrible. I'm so sorry to hear about your grandmother.
quests.contextClue: Bad news about a relative calls for sympathy.

quests.hint: The past participle of 'do'.
quests.explanation: 'Well done!' is a common way to praise someone's achievement. It is short for 'You've done well'.
quests.textToSpeak: Well ___! You finally finished the marathon.
quests.correctAnswer: Well done! You finally finished the marathon.
quests.contextClue: Finishing a marathon is an achievement to celebrate.

quests.hint: A word that makes a polite refusal or bad news sound gentler.
quests.explanation: 'I'm afraid' + clause is a polite way of giving bad news or refusing. It doesn't mean you are scared.
quests.textToSpeak: I'd love to come, but I'm ___ I already have plans that night.
quests.correctAnswer: I'd love to come, but I'm afraid I already have plans that night.
quests.contextClue: Declining an invitation politely.

quests.hint: The past participle of 'hold'.
quests.explanation: 'Get held up' means be delayed: 'held up by traffic', 'held up at work'. It is usually used in the passive.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry I'm late. The train got ___ up outside the station.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry I'm late. The train got held up outside the station.
quests.contextClue: A late arrival is explained by a train problem.

quests.hint: Decline an offer politely.
quests.explanation: 'I'll pass' politely declines an offer or invitation. It is casual and friendly.
quests.textToSpeak: Thanks for asking, but I'll have to ___ this time. I'm not feeling well.
quests.correctAnswer: Thanks for asking, but I'll have to pass this time. I'm not feeling well.
quests.contextClue: Illness explains turning something down.

quests.hint: Object to something.
quests.explanation: 'Do you mind if I + present simple' asks permission politely. A reply of 'No, go ahead' means yes, you may.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you ___ if I sit here? The other tables are all taken.
quests.correctAnswer: Do you mind if I sit here? The other tables are all taken.
quests.contextClue: The speaker asks permission to sit.

quests.hint: A modal verb used to make suggestions with 'we'.
quests.explanation: 'Shall we...?' suggests an action to a group and is very common in British English. American speakers often say 'Should we...?' or 'Let's'.
quests.textToSpeak: It's starting to rain, so ___ we get a taxi?
quests.correctAnswer: It's starting to rain, so shall we get a taxi?
quests.contextClue: A suggestion to a group as the rain begins.

quests.hint: The past form of 'be' used in advice after 'If I'.
quests.explanation: In advice with 'If I were you', we use 'were' even with 'I'. It shows an imaginary situation.
quests.textToSpeak: If I ___ you, I'd talk to your manager before making a formal complaint.
quests.correctAnswer: If I were you, I'd talk to your manager before making a formal complaint.
quests.contextClue: 'I'd talk' shows advice built on imagining being someone else.

quests.hint: Under too much pressure.
quests.explanation: 'Stressed' describes a person under pressure; 'stressful' describes the situation. So 'I'm stressed' but 'work is stressful'.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been feeling really ___ lately with all the deadlines. I can't relax.
quests.correctAnswer: I've been feeling really stressed lately with all the deadlines. I can't relax.
quests.contextClue: Deadlines and being unable to relax indicate pressure.

quests.hint: Worried and tense because something important is coming.
quests.explanation: 'Nervous about' + event is the usual pattern. It differs from 'afraid', which is for a specific danger.
quests.textToSpeak: She was so ___ about the interview that she couldn't eat breakfast.
quests.correctAnswer: She was so nervous about the interview that she couldn't eat breakfast.
quests.contextClue: An interview and no appetite point to worry.

quests.hint: Feeling bad because you think you did something wrong.
quests.explanation: 'Guilty' is the feeling of having done something wrong. 'Feel guilty about' + noun or -ing: 'guilty about forgetting'.
quests.textToSpeak: I felt so ___ when I realised I'd forgotten my sister's birthday.
quests.correctAnswer: I felt so guilty when I realised I'd forgotten my sister's birthday.
quests.contextClue: Forgetting a birthday causes remorse.

quests.hint: Believe that someone is honest and reliable.
quests.explanation: 'Trust' can be a verb ('I trust her') or a noun ('build trust'). 'Completely' emphasises it.
quests.textToSpeak: You can tell her anything. I ___ her completely.
quests.correctAnswer: You can tell her anything. I trust her completely.
quests.contextClue: 'Tell her anything' shows faith in her.

quests.hint: Someone you know a little but not well.
quests.explanation: An acquaintance is someone you know slightly; a friend is closer. Note 'an' before the vowel sound.
quests.textToSpeak: He's not really a friend, just an ___ I know from work.
quests.correctAnswer: He's not really a friend, just an acquaintance I know from work.
quests.contextClue: 'Not really a friend' shows a weaker relationship.

quests.hint: Helpful and encouraging.
quests.explanation: 'Supportive of' + decision or plan shows encouragement. 'Supportive' is the adjective and the verb is 'support'.
quests.textToSpeak: My parents have always been very ___ of my decision to study abroad.
quests.correctAnswer: My parents have always been very supportive of my decision to study abroad.
quests.contextClue: 'Always' and 'decision' signal steady encouragement.

quests.hint: Something said to make people laugh.
quests.explanation: 'It was just a joke' is a common way to say you weren't serious. The verb is also useful: 'I was joking'.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't mean to hurt your feelings. It was just a ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I didn't mean to hurt your feelings. It was just a joke.
quests.contextClue: An apology for a comment that was taken badly.

quests.hint: As if it were aimed at you as an individual.
quests.explanation: 'Take it personally' means to feel something was aimed at you. 'Don't take it personally' comforts someone.
quests.textToSpeak: Don't take it ___. He's like that with everyone.
quests.correctAnswer: Don't take it personally. He's like that with everyone.
quests.contextClue: 'Like that with everyone' shows the rudeness isn't aimed at one person.

quests.hint: The part of a situation you focus on when you want to stay positive.
quests.explanation: 'Look on the bright side' is a fixed phrase meaning think about the positive part of a bad situation.
quests.textToSpeak: Try to look on the bright ___. At least nobody got hurt.
quests.correctAnswer: Try to look on the bright side. At least nobody got hurt.
quests.contextClue: 'At least nobody got hurt' offers the positive.
